idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (unhealthy, error rate 18%). v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error after us-east, which left regions on mixed versions (us-east v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west v2.3.1). A retry finished the rollback. All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, look into the rollout orchestrator error, and find out why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
checkout-api is back on v2.3.0 in all regions and healthy, and SEV2 incident INC-0001 is open.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing (error rate 18%). v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped with an orchestrator error after only us-east had switched, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. I retried once and it finished. us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0 now, the service is healthy and the error rate is about 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 has already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the partial rollback, the retry and the current state, and it paged on-call. The first request to open it timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key. The incident list confirms there is only one incident, so on-call was paged once.

Follow-ups in the incident:
- Find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.
- Look into the rollout orchestrator error.
- Find out why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already been unhealthy in staging.
